page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.vgn6i-m16-vws.5xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor with 20 dedicated physical cores operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The system architecture is x86_64, supported by 92.0 GB of system memory, which equates to 4.6 GB per core. Acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA T4 GPU with 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is not included on this instance, and network connectivity is provisioned at a baseline bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-threaded and multi-threaded capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively low, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 10% to 25% categories. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, as demonstrated by Geekbench multi-core and PassMark CPU scores. Cryptographic and vector extensions such as AES, AVX, and AVX512f are supported, though newer instructions like AVX-512 VNNI and AMX are absent. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show average throughput, reaching 81.06 GB/sec for large block reads, while PassMark memory scores remain in the lower 25% tier.

The absence of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which must be factored into deployment architectures. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the inclusion of a dedicated NVIDIA T4 GPU alongside 20 dedicated vCPUs offers a balanced, entry-level accelerator profile without the high cost overhead of top-tier GPU hardware. This makes the instance suitable for workloads that benefit from GPU acceleration but do not require extreme single-core CPU speeds, such as ray tracing, image processing, multi-threaded data decompression, and moderate database operations.
